current.text: He is projected to come off the bench in Brooklyn's second unit.
The frontcourt is crowded. He competes with Julius Randle, Josh Minott and Danny Wolf for minutes at the four.
He did not get a contract extension, so this is a pivotal season for him.
Experts call him not a draft target. They say the Randle trade ended his fantasy value.

Brooklyn does not own its pick, so it has no reason to tank. Experts think the team may give more minutes to young players like Clowney in the second half of the season, but March minutes are uncertain.
Brooklyn plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks, 10 in total, with one playoff back-to-back. The team has 16 back-to-backs this season, tied with Boston for the most in the league.

durable.text: His shot is unreliable. He has not been an efficient three-point shooter so far, despite hot stretches.
His defensive stats and shot blocking have been inconsistent. He needs to improve his rebounding and rim protection.
He has been inconsistent and has battled injuries.

note: Clowney sits outside the draftable pool. Yahoo ranks him 230 and ESPN 269, both sites value him at 0 USD, and our league did not draft him. Neither site projects even 10 points per game, and his 39.8% FG on about 7 attempts would hurt your FG%, so he is not a target in our 144-player auction. Leave him on waivers. Check early whether he earns real minutes ahead of Minott and Wolf, and whether Brooklyn hands him a bigger role in the second half.
